sla_onsite.text: quoting for specified item. 1.4 Process Overview The following is an outline description of the process: The RTU shall be fully automated for site measurement and associated GWR SCADA reporting and shall be fully self -governed for continuous usage. All installed communication cards shall be operating on full site telemetry. Communications paths shall be to GNI Grid Control Cork and shall be through a leased telecoms line with secondary GPRS backup. Both communications circuits shall be active during normal operations. The RTU components are to be powered via 24V DC, and shall be powered by a dedicated 24V DC Battery Charger on site, which shall be sized and installed by others. In the event of a site power loss, this battery system shall maintain a secure 24V to the RTU, providing a mains fail alarm for SCADA records. Where available, a site generator shall auto start in the event of a mains failure event to provide emergency backup power for the site and RTU, providing a generator running alarm for SCADA. The new RTU shall be MODBUS capable, with allowance for new MODBUS compatible equipment to be connected to the RTU in future. This includes but is not limited to: 1. Digital Input signals 2. Digital Output signals 3. Analogue Input signals 4. Analogue O

metry is a mixture of both Digital and Analogue feedback, in both hazardous and non hazardous areas. This shall require I.S. barriers for some field telemetry, which is expanded on in the I/O requirements section of this specification. The RTU shall be capable of accepting signals directly from field mounted Pressure, Differential Pressure, and Temperature transmitters connected through intrinsically safe barriers. Input protocols for 4-20mA intrinsically safe signals include HART signals from on site transmitters. The RTU shall also be capable of measuring valve position feedback signals for pipeline transmission valves and safety slam shut valves through intrinsically safe barriers. The RTU shall also be capable of receiving digital and analogue signals from site critical equipment in non hazardous areas such as Intruder Alarm systems and site generator status signals, which shall be organised into transmittable packages by the RTU for transmission to GNI SCADA for full remote view of all site telemetry. The RTU shall be capable of communicating with additional PLCs on site and receive Modbus lists of system and process updates generated by these PLCs. Examples of this include Boiler House system communications and Flow Computer communications and USM diagnost
